descriptors.R: nominee of the party that has held a majority in the House of Representatives since 2023; a former President seeking a second, non-consecutive term
descriptors.D: the sitting Vice President, nominee of the party that has held the White House since 2021, who became the nominee after the President withdrew in July

compile_desc.R: the party that has held a majority in the House of Representatives since 2023
compile_desc.D: the party that has held the White House since 2021

others_line: Other candidates on some ballots, including a Green and a Libertarian nominee and an independent who has suspended his campaign (answer "other").
never_name: Trump, Harris, Biden, Vance, Walz, Obama, Kennedy, Stein, Chase Oliver, Cornel West, Haley, DeSantis or Pence

slice_sources.men: 2023 American Community Survey (1-year, IPUMS) aged to November 2024 along the 2022→2023 trend; men who are citizens 18+ (the native_white, naturalized, black and other slots) less those barred for a felony conviction (Sentencing Project / Uggen et al. state estimates for 2024); outside the eleven former Confederate states; turnout and choice calibrated to the certified 2024 returns.
slice_sources.women: 2023 American Community Survey (1-year, IPUMS) aged to November 2024 along the 2022→2023 trend; women who are citizens 18+ (the native_white, naturalized, black and other slots) less those barred for a felony conviction (Sentencing Project / Uggen et al. state estimates for 2024); outside the eleven former Confederate states; turnout and choice calibrated to the certified 2024 returns.
slice_sources.south-white: 2023 American Community Survey (1-year, IPUMS) aged to November 2024 along the 2022→2023 trend; white non-Hispanic adults in the eleven former Confederate states (US-born in the native_white slot; white naturalized citizens sit in the naturalized slot), less felony disenfranchisement (Sentencing Project / Uggen et al. state estimates for 2024); calibrated to the certified 2024 returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 2023 American Community Survey (1-year, IPUMS) aged to November 2024 along the 2022→2023 trend; US-born Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states, all citizens with no legal bar beyond felony disenfranchisement (Sentencing Project / Uggen et al. state estimates for 2024), which falls on them disproportionately; calibrated to the certified 2024 returns.
slice_sources.immigrants: 2023 American Community Survey (1-year, IPUMS) aged to November 2024 along the 2022→2023 trend; noncitizen adults (the alien slot), who cannot vote in federal elections; naturalized citizens are counted in the naturalized slot and can vote.
